materials.title: The signs for our classroom
materials.text:
On Saturday, our class ____1____ (make) small signs for the classroom. We wanted new students to find ordinary things without asking the teacher every time. The signs needed to be clear, not merely colourful.

We began with the storage ____2____ (box) beside the wall. One held pencils and another held paper. I drew a picture of each item and wrote the English word below it. The labels would stay ____3____ the classroom, where everyone could read them.

At first, ____4____ (I) idea was to use very pale yellow letters. They looked pretty on the desk, but my friend could not read them from the door. We changed to a darker colour and checked again.

Our teacher looked ____5____ (careful) at the spelling before we attached anything. She asked us to correct one missing letter, then gave us permission to put the signs in place. I decided ____6____ (wash) my hands before touching the clean paper because I had paint on my fingers.

We made another sign ____7____ the art cupboard. It was ____8____ (big) than the labels on the boxes because it needed to be seen across the room. Before ____9____ (put) it up, we checked that it would not cover the cupboard handle.

On Monday, a new pupil found the paper without help. She smiled at the drawings and asked if she could make ____10____ additional label for the reading corner. Our little project was not finished forever; another person had already found a useful next step.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of make.
questions.explanation: Saturday in this past narrative takes made. Base and unaided -ing do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of box.
questions.explanation: The storage boxes are multiple, including pencil and paper boxes. Box is singular and boxs is a nonstandard plural.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Labels stay in the classroom. Other listed prepositions do not express the location.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of I.
questions.explanation: My modifies idea. Personal and independent possessive forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of careful.
questions.explanation: Carefully modifies looked. Careful adjective and carefulness noun do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of wash.
questions.explanation: Decided to wash uses an infinitive. Other listed forms do not follow decided directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: A sign for the cupboard is intended for it. Of/from do not express that purpose in this setting.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of big.
questions.explanation: Than requires comparative bigger. Bigest is misspelled, biggest superlative and more bigger doubled.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of put.
questions.explanation: Before putting takes an -ing clause. Base/to-infinitive do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: An additional label begins with a vowel sound. Other article readings remain reviewable.

materials.title: Our Saturday library visit
materials.text:
My little brother ____1____ (visit) the library with me most Saturdays. He likes the children's room because there are low shelves and a table where he can look at pictures. I usually choose a longer story for myself.

The librarian helps several ____2____ (child) find books when we arrive. She does not choose every title for them. She asks what they enjoy and shows them where that kind of book is kept.

Last week, I borrowed ____3____ story about a family living beside the sea. It was not the book I had planned to choose. A picture on the cover caught ____4____ (I) attention, and the first page made me want to continue.

I enjoy ____5____ (read) near the window, but we cannot stay there all morning. My brother gets hungry before lunch. When he is ready, I put a marker in the book instead of trying to finish too ____6____ (quick).

We thank the librarian ____7____ her help before leaving. At home, I tell Mum why the new story seems ____8____ (interesting) than the one I read the week before. She asks about the characters rather than only the number of pages.

My brother ____9____ (choose) a comic last Saturday. He has looked through it many times and now wants to borrow another by the same writer. We put both books on the shelf beside the door so we can find them ____10____ the right time. Returning a book is part of borrowing it, even when we would like to keep reading.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of visit.
questions.explanation: Singular brother in a regular present habit takes visits. Visit disagrees and visiting lacks auxiliary.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of child.
questions.explanation: Several requires plural children. Child is singular and childs nonstandard.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: A story begins with consonant s. Other article readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of I.
questions.explanation: My modifies attention. Personal and independent possessive forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of read.
questions.explanation: Enjoy takes reading as the activity. Base and to-infinitive do not follow enjoy directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of quick.
questions.explanation: Quickly modifies finish. Quickness is noun; unlisted informal flat-adverb uses remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Thank for help uses for. Other listed prepositions do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of interesting.
questions.explanation: Than requires more interesting. Interestinger is nonstandard and most superlative.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of choose.
questions.explanation: Last Saturday establishes simple past chose. Present/base/unaided -ing do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: At the right time uses at. Other listed prepositions do not fit the time expression.

materials.title: The birthday clues
materials.text:
On my birthday, I ____1____ (receive) a card with a short clue inside. It did not contain money or a message naming the present. Instead, it asked me to find the place where our family kept old maps.

Dad told me ____2____ (follow) the clues in order. I went to the desk and found a folded note ____3____ was partly hidden under a notebook. The next instruction mentioned a picture of the sea, so I hurried towards the living room.

My sister asked me to be ____4____ (careful) than I had been with the first clue. There were two sea pictures in the house. One was downstairs and the other hung beside the upstairs landing. I read the wording again and noticed the reference to a small blue frame.

After ____5____ (find) the right picture, I saw another envelope behind it. The note inside directed me to look ____6____ the cupboard beside my bed. I had searched many places and had never thought of beginning in my own room.

The cupboard contained a box with several little ____7____ (surprise): a sketchbook, pencils and a ticket for an art workshop. The box ____8____ (open) only after I had read the last message aloud. Mum wanted everyone to hear why she had chosen the workshop.

The game gave ____9____ (we) a funny record of the morning. We kept the clues in ____10____ small envelope with the date on it. The present was lovely, but the wrong sea picture became the part of the story my family repeated most often.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of receive.
questions.explanation: The birthday narrative is past, so received. Base and unaided -ing do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of follow.
questions.explanation: Told me takes to follow. Other listed forms do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Note is subject antecedent of that/which was hidden. Who human, where not subject and what incompatible with the antecedent.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of careful.
questions.explanation: Than requires more careful. Most is superlative and more carefuller doubled; unlisted variants remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of find.
questions.explanation: After finding/having found both express prior discovery. Other listed forms do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Look in/inside the cupboard gives the search location. Of/from do not fit the intended placement.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of surprise.
questions.explanation: Several requires plural surprises. Singular and adjective do not fill the count slot.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of open.
questions.explanation: Singular box receives opening: was/had been opened. Opened lacks auxiliary and were disagrees.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: Gave takes object us. Subject/possessive forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: A small envelope begins with consonant s. Other article readings remain reviewable.

materials.title: The umbrellas after the festival
materials.text:
It ____1____ (rain) throughout the afternoon of the school music festival. People arrived carrying umbrellas of many colours, and the staff provided a place to leave them near the entrance. The hall itself stayed dry and warm.

My friend and I put ____2____ (we) umbrellas beside each other. Mine was plain black; hers had blue flowers. We thought remembering the colours would be enough, but many other visitors had brought black umbrellas too.

At the end, we waited ____3____ the entrance was crowded. A teacher asked everyone ____4____ (go) slowly and check before taking an item. Hurrying would not make it easier to identify similar handles and covers.

One umbrella near mine was much ____5____ (wet), although it had arrived later. Its owner had left it open in the rain while helping someone at the gate. Appearance alone did not tell us the order in which people had entered the hall.

After ____6____ (wait) for the busiest moment to pass, I found a small mark on my handle. It was ____7____ useful detail that I had forgotten when describing the umbrella only as black. My friend's blue flowers were easier to recognise from a distance.

Unclaimed umbrellas ____8____ (place) in the school's lost-property area by the staff. Clear ____9____ (direct) were added to the festival message so that families could ask about them later. We thanked the teacher ____10____ helping everyone leave with the right things. Next time, I would check a distinctive detail before the umbrella disappeared into a row of similar ones.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of rain.
questions.explanation: Past simple/progressive fit the rainy afternoon. Base and unaided -ing do not fit the finite clause.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: Our modifies umbrellas. Personal and independent possessive forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Because/as/since introduce the reason for waiting. During cannot directly introduce this finite clause.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of go.
questions.explanation: Asked everyone takes to go. Other listed forms do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of wet.
questions.explanation: Much wetter compares this umbrella with the narrator’s. Wettest is superlative and more wetter doubled.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of wait.
questions.explanation: After waiting/having waited both express prior delay. Other listed forms do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: A useful detail begins with consonant /j/. Other article readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of place.
questions.explanation: Plural umbrellas receive placement: were/had been placed. Placed lacks auxiliary and was disagrees.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of direct.
questions.explanation: Clear directions were added requires plural noun directions. Direct verb/adjective and directional adjective do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Thanked for helping uses for. Other listed prepositions do not fit.

units.alignmentNote: One complete original ten-gap form passage with seven prompted and three single-word gaps. Level/family reference only; no independent difficulty calibration.

materials.title: The room of paper clues
materials.text:
Our class joined a museum puzzle workshop in a room filled with paper clues. The guide asked us ____1____ (begin) only after she had explained the activity. Nobody was actually locked in, and the aim was to connect information rather than race towards a real escape.

One student ____2____ notebook was full of diagrams offered to record our ideas. Another read the written ____3____ (instruct) aloud. We agreed to keep the original sheets together so that a clue would not be lost among someone's belongings.

The first cards ____4____ (hide) in ordinary display folders. Finding them was easy; deciding which belonged together took longer. Two cards had similar colours but referred to different dates, so appearance was not enough.

After ____5____ (solve) the first part, we became more patient with the second. We read each sentence ____6____ (careful) than before and checked the link ____7____ two pieces of evidence instead of choosing the first possible connection.

The guide gave ____8____ (we) a small hint when we were stuck. It pointed towards a line we had already read, rather than adding a new answer. We had overlooked the importance of a word that limited the time period.

At the end, there was ____9____ explanation of the whole chain. We could see where we had reasoned well and where we had guessed. The main ____10____ (different) between our first and final attempts was not speed. It was that the final version could be explained step by step, with each claim connected to a clue the group could check.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of begin.
questions.explanation: Asked us takes to begin. Other listed forms do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Whose supplies possession before notebook. Who/which/where do not directly modify the noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of instruct.
questions.explanation: Written instructions names the guidance. Verb/adjective do not fit; unlisted singular remains reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of hide.
questions.explanation: Plural cards receive hiding: were/had been hidden. Hidden lacks auxiliary and was disagrees.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of solve.
questions.explanation: After solving/having solved both express prior completion. Other listed forms do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of careful.
questions.explanation: Than and the action read require comparative adverb more carefully. Most carefully is superlative and carefulness a noun; other unlisted informal uses remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Between relates the specified two pieces of evidence. Among indicates a larger group and of does not express this link directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: Gave takes object us. Subject/possessive forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: An explanation begins with a vowel sound. Other article readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of different.
questions.explanation: The main difference between requires a noun. Adjective/adverb do not fit.

materials.title: Once a week or twice?
materials.text:
Our school language club discussed whether it should meet once or twice a week. The teacher ____1____ (suggest) a short debate so that members could explain their reasons. We were not asked to treat the question as a contest between good and bad students.

The first task was to decide ____2____ the two plans would be compared fairly. Someone with a long journey home faced a different timetable from someone living next door to the school. The number of meetings was only part of the arrangement.

Each group was asked ____3____ (prepare) an argument and then identify a limit of its own suggestion. We listed the ____4____ (different) between the plans, including travel, preparation and opportunities to practise.

Before ____5____ (speak), we checked the information we intended to use. A claim about everyone's free afternoons could not be based only on our own diaries. Members ____6____ (ask) about their availability through a short form.

The final discussion was more useful ____7____ we had looked beyond our first preferences. One student changed her view; another kept his but explained it more clearly. A revised opinion did not count as losing the debate.

We recorded ____8____ (we) agreed trial plan: one full meeting and an optional short session for a month. It was ____9____ temporary arrangement to be reviewed later, not a promise that every future week would be identical. The teacher asked us to explain the review conditions ____10____ (clear), so we would know what information to bring back when the trial ended.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of suggest.
questions.explanation: Past simple/perfect fit the proposed debate before discussion. Base and unaided -ing do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: How the plans would be compared asks the method. Which/what do not introduce that complete passive clause as the manner question.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of prepare.
questions.explanation: Were asked takes to prepare. Other listed forms do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of different.
questions.explanation: Differences can name several contrasts, difference the overall contrast. Adjective/adverb do not fit the noun slot.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of speak.
questions.explanation: Before speaking takes an -ing clause. Other listed forms do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of ask.
questions.explanation: Plural members receive asking: were/had been asked. Asked lacks auxiliary and was disagrees.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Because/as/since introduce the research as the reason discussion improved. During cannot directly introduce this finite clause.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: Our modifies agreed trial plan. Personal and independent possessive forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: A temporary arrangement begins with consonant t. Other article readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of clear.
questions.explanation: Clearly modifies explain. Clearance is noun; unlisted flat-adverb uses remain reviewable.
